svg.aria-label: Diagram of the Barbeiro automation. Top track: launchd's plist embeds an inline bash -c command (it does not invoke run.sh, which is a separate manual entry point with the same body) every Tuesday at 11:30, which writes a timestamped header to cron.log and runs schedule_recurring.py. Auth track: get_token() first tries POST v3/login with .env email and password; on failure it falls back to reading the cached token.json key @BestBarbers:token; if that is also empty the script exits, and only then does an operator run get_token.py, which opens a persistent Playwright Chrome profile, polls localStorage every 2 seconds for up to 300 seconds for the token, and — only on success — backs up token.json to token.json.bak before overwriting it. Both auth paths converge into a single resolved token feeding next_fridays(24), which enumerates the next 24 Friday dates. For each Friday the script calls get_slots() against POST appointment/available-times and pick_hour() walks the preference ladder 09:30, 10:00, 10:30, 11:00. If no hour is free, the run bypasses booking straight to the Claude subprocess, which shells out to the Claude CLI with the Google Calendar MCP tool to create a red Tomato-colored alert event via notify_no_slot() with a 30 minute reminder, and the run stops unless --all was passed. If an hour is free, already_booked_this_week() checks GET client/appointments for an existing booking in the Monday-to-Sunday week of that Friday — GATE 2, the idempotency guard; if already booked the run skips or stops. Otherwise book() sends POST appointments/new-appointment, gated by GATE 1, the --dry-run flag, which threads through both book() and the Calendar helpers and, when true, returns the payload without sending it. On a real booking, the same Claude subprocess runs create_calendar_event() to create a Tangerine-colored event with 24 hour and 1 hour reminders. A separate, simpler CLI sibling, book.py, runs independently: it reads the same token.json, loops the next N days with --barber, --days and --services flags, and calls create_appointment() under the same --dry-run gate, but has no Calendar integration and no already-booked guard.
svg.text: write / can affect the outside world — labelled GATE n in the order it is crossed
after the script exits on empty token
none of the 4 preferred slots open

no fail-closed refresh of its own
first day with any free slot wins;
preferred hour used only as tiebreak
no Calendar write, no dedupe guard
